unit.unitTitle: Listening to the Sounds in Words

cefr.bandName: Pre-A1, before any English at all

unit.unitOverview:
No letters today. Only listening.
Some words end the same: man, pan.
Some words start the same: sun, sit.
A short word has two or three sounds.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson. Do not read.
Words: the words we use for this work.
Patterns: rhyme, first sound, counting sounds.
Listen to three short talks.
Say the sounds out loud. Record it.
Mark what you hear. No writing yet.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Hear when two words end the same
Hear when two words start the same
Count the sounds in a short word
Say the first sound in a word
Say the last sound in a word
Ask a person to say a word again

visual.lectureScript:
Hello. This is Unit 1 of Phonics.
There are no letters today. Only your ears.
Reading starts with hearing. Not with letters.
First, words that end the same.
Listen. Man. Pan.
Man. Pan. The end is the same.
We say they rhyme.
Listen again. Pin. Chin. They rhyme.
Now two that do not. Man. Cup.
Man. Cup. Not the same at the end.
Say with me. Man, pan. Rhyme.
Now the start of a word.
Listen. Sun. Sit.
Sun. Sit. The first sound is the same.
Sss. Both start with sss.
Listen. Top. Tap. Both start with t.
Now the hardest part today. Counting.
Every word is made of small sounds.
Listen to the word cat.
C. A. T. Three sounds.
Hold up a finger for each one. C. A. T.
Three fingers. Three sounds.
Now the word up. U. P. Two sounds.
Two fingers. Two sounds.
Do this many times. It gets easier.
When you can hear the sounds, you can read.
That is Unit 1. Only your ears today.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Two words that rhyme
grammar.explanation:
Words rhyme when the END is the same.
The start can be anything.
This is the first thing your ears must do.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
man  -  pan     they rhyme
pin  -  chin    they rhyme
sun  -  run     they rhyme

man  -  cup     they do NOT rhyme
sun  -  sit     they do NOT rhyme
grammar.workedExample:
You hear two words: bed and red.
1. Say them out loud, slowly.
2. Listen to the END of each one.
3. Both end -ed.
4. The ends are the same.
5. So they rhyme.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not listen to the start.
Sun and sit start the same and do NOT rhyme.
Rhyme is about the end only.
grammar.memoryTip: Rhyme is the END of the word.
grammar.practice:
Do they rhyme? Yes or no.
1. cat, hat
2. sun, run
3. man, cup
4. pin, chin
5. bed, red
6. top, tap
grammar.answerKey:
1. yes
2. yes
3. no
4. yes
5. yes
6. no
Five or six right? Your ears are working.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Two words that start the same
grammar.explanation:
Now the other end of the word.
Two words can start with the same sound.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
sun  -  sit     both start sss
top  -  tap     both start t
big  -  bag     both start b

sun  -  top     they do NOT

Say only the FIRST sound. Not the letter name.
grammar.workedExample:
You hear two words: man and milk.
1. Say the first sound of man. Mmm.
2. Say the first sound of milk. Mmm.
3. They are the same.
4. So they start the same.
5. Say: both start with mmm.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not say the letter NAME.
Not em. Say the sound: mmm.
The names come later, in Unit 2.
grammar.memoryTip: Say the sound, not the letter name.
grammar.practice:
Do they start the same? Yes or no.
1. sun, sit
2. top, tap
3. big, sun
4. man, milk
5. cup, cat
6. dog, bus
grammar.answerKey:
1. yes
2. yes
3. no
4. yes
5. yes
6. no
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Counting the sounds
grammar.explanation:
Every word is made of small sounds.
Hold up one finger for each sound.
This is the skill the whole level rests on.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
up      u-p        2 sounds
cat     c-a-t      3 sounds
stop    s-t-o-p    4 sounds

Hold up a finger for each sound.
Then sweep across them and say the word.
grammar.workedExample:
You hear the word bus.
1. Say it slowly: b-u-s.
2. One finger for b.
3. Another for u.
4. Another for s.
5. Three fingers. Three sounds.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not count the LETTERS.
You cannot see letters yet, and that is fine.
Count what you HEAR.
grammar.memoryTip: One finger for each sound you hear.
grammar.practice:
How many sounds?
1. up
2. cat
3. at
4. stop
5. bus
6. man
grammar.answerKey:
1. two
2. three
3. two
4. four
5. three
6. three
Five or six right? You are ready for letters.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: The first sound and the last
grammar.explanation:
Once you can count them, you can pick one out.
The first and the last are the easiest.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
cat     first c     last t
sun     first s     last n
up      first u     last p

The middle is hardest. That comes later.
grammar.workedExample:
You hear the word dog.
1. Say it slowly: d-o-g.
2. What came out of your mouth first? D.
3. What came last? G.
4. Say: first d, last g.
5. The middle one is o.
grammar.commonMistake:
The last sound is not always the last LETTER.
That does not matter yet. Trust your ears.
grammar.memoryTip: Say the word slowly. The answer is in your mouth.
grammar.practice:
Say the first sound.
1. sun
2. cat
3. dog
Say the last sound.
4. sun
5. cat
6. dog
grammar.answerKey:
1. s
2. c
3. d
4. n
5. t
6. g
Five or six right? Good ears.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Do they rhyme?
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Tap Listen. You will hear two words.
Say yes if they rhyme. Say no if they do not.
1. cat, hat
2. sun, run
3. man, cup
4. pin, chin
5. bed, red
6. top, tap
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: yes, yes, no, yes, yes, no.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Tap Listen. Say yes or no.
1. sun, sit
2. top, tap
3. big, sun
4. man, milk
5. cup, cat
6. dog, bus
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: yes, yes, no, yes, yes, no.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Count the sounds
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Tap Listen. Hold up a finger for each sound.
Then say the number.
1. up
2. cat
3. at
4. stop
5. bus
6. man

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 4 — First sound, last sound
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Say each word slowly. Then say its first sound.
1. sun
2. cat
3. dog
Now say the LAST sound of each.
4. sun
5. cat
6. dog
Tap the mic. Say six sounds.
Check: s, c, d, then n, t, g.
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor for a word. Say its first sound and its last.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Ask for it again
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
You did not hear the word. Ask.
1. Again, please.
2. Slowly, please.
3. Sorry? One more time.
4. Can you say it slowly?
Tap the mic. Say all four.
Use these every time you are not sure. That is not failing.
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor to say a word fast. Then ask it to slow down.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Say it slowly, then fast
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Say each word two ways.
First slowly, sound by sound.
Then fast, as one word.
1. c-a-t ... cat
2. b-u-s ... bus
3. m-a-n ... man
4. s-u-n ... sun
Tap the mic. Say all four both ways.
Check: did the slow one have separate sounds?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor to say a word slowly. Say it back fast.

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 1 — Mark what you hear
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Do not write letters today.
Make one mark for each sound you hear.
Use a line, like this: | | |
writing.successCriteria:
One mark for each sound.
Two marks for up.
Three marks for cat.
Four marks for stop.
writing.extension: Now do the same for your own name.

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 2 — Draw a line between the ones that rhyme
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Two lists. Join each word on the left
to the word on the right that rhymes with it.
writing.modelText:
man ......... run
pin ......... pan
sun ......... chin
writing.successCriteria:
Three lines.
Each one joins a rhyming pair.
man goes to pan. pin goes to chin. sun goes to run.
writing.extension: Say each pair out loud after you join it.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 6 — Which one does not fit?
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Three words. Two rhyme. Find the one that does not.
1. cat, hat, sun
2. pin, chin, bus
3. man, cup, pan
4. red, bed, dog
5. top, tap, map
activities.answerSummary:
1. sun
2. bus
3. cup
4. dog
5. top
Four or five right: you can hear rhyme without being told.
Number 5 is the hard one: tap and map rhyme, top does not.
activities.soloPath: Say all three out loud, then choose.

assignments.title: Listening: rhyme, first sounds, counting
assignments.instructions:
One part, all spoken. There is nothing to write.
Record yourself doing three things.
1. Say three pairs of words that rhyme.
2. Say two words that start with the same sound.
3. Say these words slowly and count the sounds:
up, cat, bus, stop.
Listen back before you finish.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: No letters, and that is deliberate
teacherNotes.note: Cambridge's Workbook A opens with rhyme and initial sounds before any letter, and this unit keeps that. An adult who cannot hear that man and pan end alike cannot be taught to blend, and every later unit rests on it. If a learner asks for letters, tell them Unit 2 is next week's work and this is what makes it possible.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.note: Mmm, not em. Sss, not ess. A learner who learns the names first has to unlearn them to blend, because em-ay-pee will never make map. Correct it here, gently, every time.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: Phonic fingers are the technique to teach
teacherNotes.note: One finger per sound, then sweep the other index finger across them and say the whole word. It is from the workbook's own teaching notes and it externalises the counting so you can see whether the learner has it.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: An adult may find this unit embarrassing
teacherNotes.note: It looks like a game and it is not. Say out loud what it is for: every literate person did this once, most of them at five, and doing it at forty is the same work at a worse moment. Then move briskly.

2. bus
3. cup
4. dog
5. top
Four or five right: you can hear rhyme without being told.
Number 5 is the hard one: tap and map rhyme, top does not.
